title: Operator Annotations and Trace Harmonization — Checklist & Notes
content:
Purpose
This note captures a compact, operational checklist and design notes for adding structured operator annotations to traces and harmonizing trace fields across services. Goal: make dashboards, root-cause flows, and incident timelines more actionable and reduce time-to-annotated-evidence during incidents.

Context / motivation
- We have high variance in how services attach metadata to spans (user vs. customer vs. tenant ids; model metadata; fallback reasons).
- Dashboards and post-incident timelines often require manual joins across logs, traces, and metrics.
- Add structured operator annotations that are lightweight (few kb) and standardized so dashboards can surface an "annotation layer" (deploys, canaries, incidents, throttles, capacity changes).

Definitions (what I mean by terms)
- Operator annotation: short JSON blob added to the trace root span or propagated as an event that contains operational context (deploy id, rollout tag, capacity tier, operator note id).
- Harmonization: agreed canonical names and types for high-value trace attributes across services and runtimes.
- Annotation layer: time-series/trace overlay in dashboards that shows operator events annotated on latency/cost panels.

Core annotation schema (proposal, keep tiny)
- ann.type: string (values: deploy, canary, incident, config-change, test-run, maintenance)
- ann.id: string (unique operator event id e.g. OP-2025-0042)
- ann.severity: string (info|warn|critical) — optional
- ann.actor: string (team or user who triggered it)
- ann.details: string (free-text, 140 char max)
- ann.started_at: iso8601 timestamp (optional for long ops)
- ann.meta: comma-separated kv pairs (limited to 140 chars)
- propagated_keys: list-of-strings in metadata (e.g., session_id, request_id) — store as comma list in ann.meta to avoid nested objects

Immutable trace attributes to standardize (must exist on root/span where appropriate)
- request_id (trace-level UUID) -> key: request_id
- session_id -> session_id
- tenant_id -> tenant_id (for multi-tenant routing and cost attribution)
- model_variant -> model_variant (e.g. redwood-1.1-q4)
- route -> route (api route or logical handler)
- kv_cache_hit -> kv_cache_hit (boolean as 0/1)
- batching_size -> batch_sz (int)
- fallback_reason -> fallback_reason (string code)
- hw_tier -> hw_tier (e.g., a100-80, gpusmall-rt)

Why these fields?
- They answer the most common investigation questions: which tenant, which model, whether cache/batching was used, and whether a fallback happened.

Usage patterns / where to attach annotations
- attach ann.* to root span on operator actions (deploys/rollouts) and to a synthetic probe span for canaries
- for per-request operational inference (like an internal fallback), attach fallback_reason and kv_cache_hit on the request span
- persist ann.* in tracing backends and index a subset (ann.type, ann.id, ann.started_at, ann.actor) for fast query

Sampling & retention guidance
- Sampling should preserve 1:1 for traces that contain ann.* (i.e., never drop an annotated trace)
- For ordinary traffic, keep default adaptive sampling (retain low-latency representative set + all high-error/high-latency traces)
- Retention: keep annotated traces for 90 days; keep metric-aggregates forever per retention policy

Dashboard overlay notes (how dashboards should consume annotations)
- Every latency/cost dashboard should have an "annotation layer" toggle that queries ann.type in the trace index and overlays event markers with hover text from ann.details
- Panels to include: model-variant timeline, fallback-rate, kv-cache-hit-rate, median P95 token latency broken down by hw_tier
- Annotation colors: deploy=blue, canary=purple, incident=red, maintenance=yellow, config-change=orange
- Default hover template: "[ann.started_at] ann.type ann.id — ann.actor: ann.details"

Metric derivations from trace fields (simple formulas)
- kv_cache_hit_rate = sum(kv_cache_hit==1) / count(requests) per tenant
- fallback_rate = sum(fallback_reason != '') / count(requests) per model_variant
- tokens_per_request = sum(tokens_generated)/count(requests)
- effective_qps_by_variant = count(requests)/window_seconds filtered by model_variant + hw_tier

Alerting heuristics (starter set)
- kv_cache_hit_rate drop: alert when drop > 25% relative to a 7d baseline and absolute < 45% for 10m
- fallback_rate spike: alert if fallback_rate increases 3x over baseline for 5m and absolute rate > 0.5% for production tenants
- P95 latency regression: alert when P95 increases by >40% vs 6h moving baseline and breach > 1500ms for any customer-facing route

Instrumentation checklist (for engineers adding fields)
- add standardized key on root span only (request_id, session_id, tenant_id)
- add model_variant + batch_sz + kv_cache_hit on inference-span
- ensure fallback_reason is emitted as a span tag and as a log line with the same request_id
- do not attach large blobs to traces; use ann.meta for small kv pairs only
- unit-tests: assert that annotated traces include ann.type and ann.id for operator actions

Operational runbook snippets
- When doing a canary rollout: create operator annotation OP-<id> with ann.type=canary, ann.meta=target-tenant:alpha, started_at set. Ensure SDK call instr.record_annotation(op_event)
- For emergency incident: SRE creates ann.type=incident with ann.severity=critical and sets ann.details to "rollback to vX until fix". Dashboard shows immediate red marker.

Implementation notes and examples (pseudo-code)
- python snippet (conceptual):
  def record_operator_annotation(tracer, type, id, actor, details, meta=None, started_at=None):
      span = tracer.get_root_span()
      ann = f"type={type},id={id},actor={actor},details={details},meta={meta or ''},started_at={started_at or now()}"
      span.set_tag('ann', ann)  # single tag to keep index small

- trace ingestion: telemetry pipeline should parse ann tag by splitting on commas and index ann.type, ann.id, ann.started_at

Open questions / tradeoffs
- nested JSON vs single-tag CSV: single-tag easier to index today but less structured; nested JSON is cleaner but increases storage/indexing cost. Proposal: keep single-tag canonical for now and evolve if index cost allowed.
- propagation cost: how much extra header/data do we allow through client SDKs? keep ann small and only attach when operator action triggered.
- visibility for Private deployments: ensure ann.* keys are configurable so customers can map to their tenant_id naming scheme

Next steps / action items
- engineering-observability: prototype ann parsing in ingestion (owner: Marcus Li) — JIRA-OBS-778
- serving-runtime: add standard tag names to SDK + small unit tests (owner: Ethan Ramirez) — due 2025-03-15
- dashboards: wire annotation overlay on latency dashboard (owner: Zoe Martinez) — sketch due 2025-03-01

Notes-to-self (loose)
- keep annotation blobs < 300 bytes max
- make ann.id deterministic format OP-YYYYMM-NNN  (helps search)
- ensure we can map ann.id -> internal incident/ticket systems (link in ann.meta)

References
- see linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412 for ingestion parser prototype
- related confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-obs-annotations-2025

End.
